$comment: Canonical GENOSYS design tokens. This file is the source of truth for the
values shared by the website (cosmetics-website) and the mobile app
(genosys-mobile-app).
The two live in separate git repositories, so there is no build-time import
between them. Instead an identical copy of this file is committed to each,
and each repo has a check that asserts its own native token definition still
matches this file:
website    npm run verify:tokens   ->  scripts/verify-design-tokens.mjs
mobile app npm run verify:tokens   ->  scripts/verify-design-tokens.mjs
Both checks also compare `version` and the sha256 in `.tokens-checksum`, so a
change made in one repo and not carried to the other is caught rather than
silently drifting. Before this file existed the palette was kept in sync by
hand, which had already let one border grey drift apart unnoticed.
To change a token: edit here, run the generator note in each repo's check
output, update both repos, bump `version`.

color.$comment: The cera palette. Website: --cera-* in app/globals.css. App: `cera` export in utils/theme.js.

$comment: Success / info / warning / destructive, and the washed panel and border
tones behind each. The app arrived at these first: the stock iOS and
Tailwind status colours read cold against cream and several failed
contrast outright, so each was deepened until it clears 4.5:1 on cream
and takes white at 5:1 or better where it backs a filled control.
The website had no named status colours at all and used raw Tailwind
utilities, which is how text-green-600 (3.09:1 on cream) and a green-500
Add to Bag button (2.28:1 under white) shipped. Website: --status-* in
app/globals.css. App: the matching keys on `colors` in utils/theme.js.
`red` is listed here for completeness; both surfaces already agreed on it.
Third-party marks, kept out of `status` because they are not ours to
retune. WhatsApp's #25D366 is the recognised mark and belongs on its own
tile, but it only reaches 1.98:1 under white so it cannot back a filled
button; `whatsappDeep` is the official dark variant and clears 7.67:1.
`whatsappHover` is one step darker again, so these buttons keep a hover
state instead of collapsing to a single flat colour.

eyebrow.$comment: Uppercase kicker above section titles. Appears on product pages on both surfaces, so a mismatch here is directly visible when comparing them side by side.

$comment: Sans section heading. The website sizes it fluidly and the app fixes it,
so only the phone-width result is shared here. The web's clamp yields a
preferred 13.8px at a 390px viewport, meaning its 24px floor was doing
all the work and had never been tuned for phones; the app's 20px was a
deliberate choice. The web now comes down to meet it under 640px.
Above 640px the website is free to grow this fluidly to 30px; that is
out of scope for a phone-shared token.
